data.hypothesis: Test an intermediate 160-thread CTA/source tile with compact 16-byte shared source records. Prior measurements found the compact 128-thread version valid at 0.00089008 s and the compact 192-thread version valid at 0.00092263 s; the 96-thread version was slower at 0.00098055 s. With seven distinct prior programs and no repeats, this five-warp configuration tests whether fewer source-tile iterations than at 128 threads can offset a larger CTA and 2,560-byte shared allocation. No speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: CTA source tiling with one target per thread; compare tile sizes under the same official protocol.
memory_lessons.claim: The compact 128-thread trial was faster than the compact 192-thread trial in the supplied measurements, but this does not establish the best tile size or explain the difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a distinct intermediate 160-thread CTA/tile after correctness passes.

data.notes: The supplied baseline is valid at 0.00184441 s. Earlier role results report seven distinct programs across seven trials, with no repeats; the measurements above are historical candidates, not a measurement of this proposal. The source loop preserves ascending interaction order, both CTA barriers include threads without valid targets, partial source tiles are bounded, and output writes are guarded. The controller should complete all correctness checks before timing; no result is claimed for this candidate.
transformations: Set block and items_per_block to 160, maintaining exactly one target per thread and a matching 160-source CTA tile.
Stage only source position and mass in a dynamic shared array of compact records, using 2,560 bytes.
Retain ascending source interaction order, barriers around each staged tile, partial-tile bounds, and guards for target reads and output writes.
